suggestions: convert INTERSECT to UNION ALL with channel discriminator
replace distinct with group by and count distinct
optimized_sql:
SELECT count(*)
FROM (
    SELECT customer.c_last_name, customer.c_first_name, sales_channels.d_date
    FROM (
        SELECT store_sales.ss_customer_sk AS customer_sk, date_dim.d_date, 1 AS channel
        FROM store_sales
        JOIN date_dim ON store_sales.ss_sold_date_sk = date_dim.d_date_sk
        WHERE date_dim.d_month_seq BETWEEN 1189 AND 1189 + 11
        GROUP BY store_sales.ss_customer_sk, date_dim.d_date
        UNION ALL
        SELECT catalog_sales.cs_bill_customer_sk AS customer_sk, date_dim.d_date, 2 AS channel
        FROM catalog_sales
        JOIN date_dim ON catalog_sales.cs_sold_date_sk = date_dim.d_date_sk
        WHERE date_dim.d_month_seq BETWEEN 1189 AND 1189 + 11
        GROUP BY catalog_sales.cs_bill_customer_sk, date_dim.d_date
        UNION ALL
        SELECT web_sales.ws_bill_customer_sk AS customer_sk, date_dim.d_date, 3 AS channel
        FROM web_sales
        JOIN date_dim ON web_sales.ws_sold_date_sk = date_dim.d_date_sk
        WHERE date_dim.d_month_seq BETWEEN 1189 AND 1189 + 11
        GROUP BY web_sales.ws_bill_customer_sk, date_dim.d_date
    ) AS sales_channels
    JOIN customer ON customer.c_customer_sk = sales_channels.customer_sk
    GROUP BY customer.c_last_name, customer.c_first_name, sales_channels.d_date
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT sales_channels.channel) = 3
) AS hot_cust
LIMIT 100

reasoning_trace:
1. COMBINE INTERSECT LEGS — TARGET: the three DISTINCT+INTERSECT subqueries over store_sales/catalog_sales/web_sales joined to date_dim and customer — TRANSFORMATION: replace the whole chain with a single UNION ALL of the three sales arms tagged with channel constants, then GROUP BY (c_last_name,c_first_name,d_date), HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT channel)=3, and COUNT the groups; this removes the redundant per-leg DISTINCT sorts and the two INTERSECT passes.

2. PUSH DATE FILTER INTO EACH BRANCH — TARGET: date_dim.d_month_seq and the sold-date keys ss_sold_date_sk/cs_sold_date_sk/ws_sold_date_sk — TRANSFORMATION: in each UNION ALL arm, join date_dim and apply d_month_seq BETWEEN 1189 AND 1200 before the UNION is formed, so only the 12-month window rows reach the customer join and final grouping.

3. PRE-AGGREGATE BRANCH ROWS — TARGET: store_sales(ss_customer_sk,ss_sold_date_sk), catalog_sales(cs_bill_customer_sk,cs_sold_date_sk), web_sales(ws_bill_customer_sk,ws_sold_date_sk) — TRANSFORMATION: collapse each date-filtered arm to distinct (customer_sk, d_date, channel tag) before joining customer, and let the final GROUP BY on (c_last_name,c_first_name,d_date) enforce the set semantics; this cuts the customer join and final hash input.

4. ADD SUPPORTING INDEXES — TARGET: the date+customer join/aggregation keys of all three sales tables — TRANSFORMATION: create composite B-tree indexes on store_sales(ss_sold_date_sk, ss_customer_sk), catalog_sales(cs_sold_date_sk, cs_bill_customer_sk), and web_sales(ws_sold_date_sk, ws_bill_customer_sk) so the date-filtered branch scans avoid full 57M/29M/14M relation scans.
